review: 1:1–6 is the six-line opening stanza (88.88.88 against the print's 88.88), kept whole because it is the hymn's charge: the three 'who' clauses address the same people the Arabic addresses three times (يَا مَنْ … يَا مَنْ … يَا مَنْ), and the imperative lands only at line 4.

1:4–6 אֱהָבוּ … תְּנוּ — the Arabic حُبُّوا كَمَا أُحْبِبْتُمُ / أَعْطُوا كَمَا أُعْطِيتُمُ is the golden-rule pattern; the Hebrew keeps the passive 'as you were loved/given' with the same verbs, and adds הָשִׁיבוּ לָאָב הֵד for 'echo to the Father', since הֵד is the biblical echo-word of Job 37:4 (קוֹל יִשָּׁמֵעַ).

2:1–2 מֵאֵל אֲשֶׁר לֹא־שְׁכָחַנִי — the Arabic مِنْ خَالِقٍ لَمْ يَنْسَنِي is 'from a Creator who did not forget me'; the relative clause is kept as a relative clause, so the love is located in an act of remembering, which is the psalm's category (Ps 9:13, לֹא־שָׁכַח).

2:3–4 הֵרִיק … מִתְרוֹשֵׁשׁ וְהוּא הֶעָשִׁיר — Phil 2:7 with 2 Cor 8:9 (כִּי־עָשִׁיר הָיָה, בַּעֲבוּרְכֶם הֶעֱנִי); the two halves of the verse are kept in the two lines in the same order as the Arabic (أَخْلَى … مُفْتَقِرًا وَهوَ الْغَنِيّ).

4:2 בָּאַהֲבָה אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם — the Arabic صَبْرٌ وَاحْتِمَال is 'patience and endurance'; the Hebrew uses the single biblical phrase אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם (Exod 34:6, אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם וְרַב־חֶסֶד), which covers both the bearing and the long-suffering, because two separate nouns overran the tune's nine syllables.

4:4 חֶסֶד וְכָבוֹד לֹא יָסוּרוּ — the Arabic فَضْلٌ وَمَجْدٌ لَا يُزَال is 'favour and glory that are not removed'; סוּר is the biblical verb of departing (1 Sam 16:14), and the negative is kept so the line promises permanence rather than merely praising.
